task: Explore: build a Lomb-Scargle periodogram tool for unevenly sampled data (research algorithms as tools, 17th)
errors: astropy 6.1.4 failed to import with numpy 2.3 (np.in1d removed); pinned numpy 2.1.3, then Baluev FAP needed scipy (1.14.1)
First FAP comparison was 2.3e-6 relative off astropy: astropy snaps maximum_frequency onto its own grid (0.5000012 for 0.5); the fixture now records the snapped value and agreement is 3e-10
Error-column name regex matched any column starting with 'e' (e.g. 'energy'); tightened and tested

notes: Idea: Lomb-Scargle periodogram (generalised, error-weighted, one offset per group) with Baluev FAP, pre-whitening and spectral-window alias check, as a research-algorithm tool; none existed for uneven sampling. Verified against astropy 6.1.4 (power 1e-9, FAP 1e-8 rel), brute-force least squares with groups (1e-10), synthetic recovery and an aliasing case. On Fulton et al. 2016's 401 HD 164922 velocities (radvel example, MIT) with jitter 2.6 it finds 1196.96, 75.75, 12.47, 41.75 d: the periods of planets b, c, d (Benatti 2020) and e (Rosenthal 2021), literature checked by web search; framed as a retrospective check, the 5th peak (4.71 d) flagged as not a known planet and settings-dependent. Browser check at 1100 and 390 px: no errors, no external requests, no overflow. Local: node --test 35/35; venture-preflight clean on the third run (build + check.mjs + site and privacy tests); run_venture_tests.py lomb-scargle-periodogram robust-pca: 2 suites, 0 failed. No agent doc in docs/reports: the venture README and research-tools README carry what the next run needs.
